location: Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja
title: Prof. Tijjani Bande hails CSOs' role in national development, says civil society is now key to modern governance
excerpt: Former UNGA President Prof. Tijjani Muhammad Bande told the NCSOS Summit 2026 that civil society has moved from being seen as opposition to government to becoming a central partner in governance.
story: At the National Civil Society Organisations Summit 2026, former UNGA President Prof. Tijjani Muhammad Bande commended the NCSOS/CSCHEI organizers for convening diverse stakeholders to drive the Nigeria First agenda.

Speaking on the evolving role of civil society, he noted that civil society has moved from being seen as opposition to government to becoming a central partner in governance, critical to achieving the SDGs and tackling global challenges like climate change, health and security.

location: Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja
title: Panelist urges CSOs to focus on food security and support real rural farmers to accelerate SDGs
excerpt: At the NCSOS Summit 2026 panel on SDGs, a panelist urged CSOs to move beyond advocacy and prioritize food security by supporting advanced subsistence farmers in rural communities.
story: At the National Civil Society Organisations Summit 2026 with the theme Nigeria First, held at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja, a panel session on How Civil Society Can Accelerate Implementation of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at National and Sub-National Levels called for practical action on food security.
Speaking during the session, a panelist said civil society must go beyond pushing for good governance to proffering practical solutions to Nigeria's macro-economic challenges.
According to him, one major solution that can help Nigeria reduce excessive borrowing is fixing food security.
He described Nigeria's current food security status as Amber, neither Red nor Green, noting that while government is making efforts, it is focusing on the wrong actors.

He distinguished between two categories of farmers: the advanced subsistence farmers in rural communities who actually feed the nation but do not call themselves agripreneurs, and the so-called agripreneurs whom he described as "paper tigers."

He therefore urged that agricultural budgets and interventions by government, CSOs and development partners be deliberately targeted at boosting farming activities in rural areas, where real farming takes place.
The panel featured five discussants, including the moderator. The summit was organized by NCSOS and CSCHEI, led by Amb. Kunle Yusuff, with CASNAGGI among over 5,000 participating CSOs.

location: Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja
title: Cleric urges timely release of election funds, says democracy fails when votes don't count
excerpt: At NCSOS Summit 2026, Pastor Edewor Egedegbe warned that late funding for INEC increases the risk of avoidable failures ahead of 2027, saying an election is not a war and an opponent is not an enemy.
story: At the National Civil Society Organisations Summit 2026 themed Nigeria First, held at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja, Pastor Edewor Egedegbe called for urgent measures to safeguard electoral integrity ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Speaking on the topic of electoral integrity, Pastor Egedegbe said the credibility of elections requires transparent procedures, impartial officials and effective channels for complaints.

According to him, equipment must be procured on time, tested and deployed, personnel adequately trained and materials delivered, noting that late funding can disrupt these tasks and money released later cannot always recover lost preparation time.

He cited recent experience in the Osun off-cycle election, where late court decisions affected preparations, stressing that while a funding shortfall does not automatically mean an election will be compromised, it increases the risk of avoidable failures.

He therefore urged government to urgently release any outstanding election funds, while INEC should publish what it has received and provide dated updates on procurement, testing, training and deployment of personnel to avoid speculation.

On election conflict and violence prevention, he warned that delayed voting, missing materials and inadequate personnel can create frustration and fuel accusations, adding that while security officers can maintain law and order, they cannot replace missing election materials.

He called on political actors to promote issue-based campaigns, community leaders to encourage tolerance and civility, security agencies and civil society to identify threats early, and the media and citizens to verify information before sharing to avoid fake news.
"Election is not a war. And a political opponent is not also an enemy. These two things must find full expression in our heart," he said.
In conclusion, he said credible and peaceful elections are built long before polling day, urging citizen education, timely funding, strengthened accountability and violence prevention.

"Let's stop agonizing and start organizing going forward as a people and as a country. Our democracy succeeds when votes count, when lives are protected, and citizens participate in the electoral process without fear or intimidation," he added.
The summit was organized by NCSOS and CSCHEI, led by Amb. Kunle Yusuff, with CASNAGGI among over 5,000 participating CSOs.

location: Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja
title: National Civil Society Organizations Summit 2026: Nigeria First
excerpt: CSO leaders from across Nigeria's 774 local government areas met in Abuja under the theme Nigeria First, renewing their commitment to work with the Federal Government as partners in governance ahead of the 2027 general elections.
story: The National Civil Society Organizations Summit 2026, held at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja, under the theme Nigeria First, brought together CSO leaders and stakeholders from across the 774 Local Government Areas of Nigeria.

Call to action: Civil Society Organizations reaffirmed their commitment to stronger citizens' participation, accountable governance, and deeper collaboration between government and non-state actors as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections.

Federal Government position: The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Sen. George Akume, stated that government alone cannot move Nigeria from reforms to prosperity. He called for a more robust multi-stakeholder partnership in which civil society serves as co-creators and strategic partners in governance, noting that this model is already working through Nigeria's EITI and the Open Government Partnership (OGP).

Convener's position: According to the Convener, Comrade Kunle Yusuff, the Summit was organized to ensure every Nigerian reaffirms loyalty to the country and promotes the Nigeria First agenda. He emphasized that everything that promotes peace, security, national unity, sustainable development, climate financing, electoral integrity and information integrity is about Nigeria First, with the ultimate goal of taking Nigeria from poverty to prosperity.
Focus of the Summit: strengthening democratic governance, information integrity, national unity, electoral integrity and sustainable national development.

In summary, the Summit marks a renewed commitment by CSOs and the Federal Government to work together as partners to promote the Nigeria First agenda for national development towards 2027. CASNAGGI was proud to be among the participating organizations.

title: Cash Gifts for Vulnerable Families & Orphans
excerpt: A compassionate January gathering at Nobis Hall where CASNAGGI distributed cash gifts to orphans and vulnerable families, restoring a little hope at the start of the year.
story: On a crisp January morning in Taraba State, CASNAGGI gathered at Nobis Hall, Jalingo, for what began as a simple cash-gift distribution — and quickly became a statement about the kind of Nigeria we are building, one where the most vulnerable are seen, counted and supported.

Orphans, widows and struggling families received direct cash gifts to help cover school fees, food and essential household needs. For many, the assistance arrived at the exact moment the new year's pressures were settling in.

Our volunteers also spent time listening — recording each household's situation so we can layer in follow-up support throughout 2026 through the Hope & Healing Initiative and the Community Relief Outreach.

title: Community Relief Outreach – Taraba State
excerpt: Over 500 families supported with food items, hygiene kits and essentials. Women-led groups received starter packs to launch small businesses.
story: Taraba State welcomed CASNAGGI's largest humanitarian drive of 2025. Over the course of the outreach, more than 500 vulnerable households received food items, hygiene kits and essential supplies calibrated to last a family of five through a full month.

We intentionally designed the event around women-led cooperatives. Alongside relief packages, we distributed starter packs — sewing machines, catering equipment and capital stock — to 45 women ready to turn their skills into income. It's our conviction that relief works best when paired with the tools of independence.
Community leaders, traditional rulers and local policymakers joined the closing session, turning a distribution event into a public accountability moment.

title: Free Medical Outreach — Minna & Yenagoa
excerpt: 650 beneficiaries received maternal health services, malaria screening and free essential drugs across two days of mobile clinics.
story: Our flagship Health on Wheels programme made landfall in two states — Niger and Bayelsa — delivering free primary care to communities far from the nearest clinic.

650 people received services ranging from malaria screening and anti-malarial treatment to antenatal checks, blood pressure monitoring and diabetes screening. Essential drugs were provided at no cost, with follow-up referrals for patients needing specialist care.

Dr. Chima Ikoro, CASNAGGI Board Chairman and Consultant Gynaecologist at Federal Medical Centre Yenagoa, led the maternal health station — a reminder that our board is not just strategic but hands-on.

title: Youth for Good Governance Forum (YG2F)
excerpt: 200+ young people engaged in civic education, leadership training and mentorship. 30 fellows selected for the inaugural Youth for Good Governance Fellowship.
story: We don't believe Nigeria's youth are 'leaders of tomorrow' — we believe they are leaders right now. The Youth for Good Governance Forum was designed to give them the floor.

Over 200 young people from Bayelsa, Niger and the FCT converged for two days of civic education, leadership training, and direct dialogue with policymakers. Workshops covered electoral participation, policy advocacy, digital organising and ethical leadership.

At the forum's close, 30 outstanding participants were selected as the inaugural cohort of the Youth for Good Governance Fellowship (YG2F) — a 12-month programme pairing each fellow with a governance mentor.

title: Public Dialogue on Transparency & Accountability
excerpt: Over 100 citizens, women and civil servants joined an open-air dialogue with policymakers and traditional leaders on inclusive governance.
story: Under the open sky in Bayelsa State, CASNAGGI convened a cross-section of Nigerian society — community members, women's groups, traditional rulers, civil servants and elected officials — for a direct, unscripted dialogue on transparency and accountability.

The session deliberately removed the usual barriers of protocol. Citizens asked pointed questions about service delivery, public spending and local development priorities. Officials responded, and — crucially — committed to follow-up actions monitored by CASNAGGI's Transparency Watch programme.
Over 100 participants joined. Many stayed two hours past the scheduled close.

title: Grassroots Volunteer Mobilization
excerpt: 50 youth and women volunteers trained and onboarded as community focal points, strengthening CASNAGGI's grassroots presence across three states.
story: CASNAGGI's grassroots network tripled in a single week. 50 youth and women volunteers from Taraba, Niger State and the FCT were trained and deployed as community focal points — the people neighbours call first when they need help.

Training covered outreach logistics, data collection, safeguarding, civic education facilitation and the CASNAGGI code of ethics. Every volunteer received a CASNAGGI-branded kit and a clear reporting structure to the state coordinator.
The network will anchor our 2026 field operations across humanitarian response, civic education and women's enterprise.

title: 150 Women & Youth Graduate Vocational Training
excerpt: Tailoring, ICT and catering cohort graduates 150. 45 participants received sewing machines, hairdressing tools and catering equipment to begin earning immediately.
story: Graduation days at CASNAGGI don't end with certificates. They end with tools.

150 women and youth completed intensive vocational training across tailoring, ICT and catering streams. At the ceremony, 45 of the most entrepreneur-ready graduates received start-up kits — sewing machines, catering equipment and ICT bundles — enabling income generation from day one.

This cohort represents the first wave of the She Leads Project x Women in Enterprise pipeline. Follow-up check-ins at 3, 6 and 12 months will track their business outcomes and loop the highest performers back in as peer mentors.

title: Board of Trustees Inaugural Strategy Meeting
excerpt: The CASNAGGI Board of Trustees convened its first strategy meeting, adopting the 2025–2035 Strategic Action Plan and operational governance framework.
story: Every national movement needs a serious first meeting. Ours happened one week after CAC registration, at the Bayelsa head office.

Founder/CEO Comrade Ifeoma Okorie Ikoro, Board Chairman Dr. Chima Ikoro and the Directors convened for two days of strategic planning. The board adopted the 2025–2035 Strategic Action Plan, approved the governance and financial management policies, and set the operational calendar for the first 12 months.
Minutes, resolutions and the adopted strategic document are archived with the Corporate Affairs Commission and available to institutional partners on request.

title: CASNAGGI Officially Registered (RC: 8722526)
excerpt: CASNAGGI secured legal registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission of Nigeria as a non-profit, non-governmental organization — our founding day.
story: On 21 August 2025, Care Support for the Needy and Good Governance Initiative was formally incorporated with the Corporate Affairs Commission of Nigeria under registration number RC: 8722526.

Registration formalised years of informal work into a national legal vehicle — enabling CASNAGGI to enter into institutional partnerships, receive grants and publish audited accounts under Nigerian non-profit regulations.
It is also the date we now consider our founding anniversary — and a reminder that accountability starts with being a legally accountable entity before you ask others to be accountable.
